final_note: You worked through Electromagnetic waves: Visible light (physics only) — 9 specification statements.

concepts.def: The band of electromagnetic waves that the human eye can detect, running from red at one end to violet at the other. It is a continuous spectrum: the colours run into one another rather than being separated by gaps.

concepts.term: Narrow band of wavelength and frequency
concepts.def: Each colour within the visible light spectrum has its own narrow band of wavelength and frequency. A colour such as red is therefore not one single wavelength but a small range of wavelengths, with a matching small range of frequencies.

concepts.term: Order of colours by wavelength and frequency
concepts.def: Across the visible spectrum, red light has the longest wavelength and the lowest frequency and violet light has the shortest wavelength and the highest frequency. Because all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed through a vacuum, a longer wavelength always corresponds to a lower frequency.
Reflection from a smooth surface in a single direction. Parallel rays arriving at a smooth surface, such as a mirror or still water, leave it still parallel, so a clear image can be seen.

Reflection from a rough surface causes scattering: this is called diffuse reflection. Parallel rays arriving at a rough surface, such as paper or matt paint, are reflected in many different directions, so no clear image is formed.

concepts.term: Law of reflection in diffuse reflection
concepts.def: Diffuse reflection does not break the law of reflection. At every point on a rough surface the angle of incidence still equals the angle of reflection; the surface is uneven, so the normals at neighbouring points face in different directions and the reflected rays are scattered.

A material that works by absorbing certain wavelengths (and colour) and transmitting other wavelengths (and colour). A red filter transmits red light and absorbs the other wavelengths; it does not create or add colour.
Light passing through a material and out the other side. Transmitted light is not changed into a different colour: its wavelength is the same on leaving the material as it was on entering.

Light energy being taken in by a material rather than being reflected or transmitted by it. Wavelengths that a filter or an opaque object absorbs do not reach the eye, so they make no contribution to the colour that is seen.

The colour of an opaque object is determined by which wavelengths of light are more strongly reflected. Wavelengths that are not reflected are absorbed, so a blue object reflects blue light strongly and absorbs the rest.

If all wavelengths are reflected equally the object appears white. A white object under white light therefore sends every wavelength back to the eye, which is why it takes on the colour of any coloured light shone on it.
If all wavelengths are absorbed the object appears black. Light does reach a black object; almost none of it is reflected back to the eye, so no colour is seen.

An object that transmits light without scattering it, so light passes through in a single direction and objects behind it can be seen clearly. Clear window glass and still, clean water are transparent.
An object that transmits light but scatters it as it passes through, so light gets through but objects behind it cannot be seen clearly. Frosted glass, tracing paper and thin fabric are translucent.
An object that transmits no light. Light falling on it is either reflected or absorbed, and it is the balance of those two that fixes the colour the object appears.

The idea that one object treats different wavelengths of light differently: it may reflect some strongly, absorb others and transmit others. The colour seen depends on which wavelengths actually reach the eye, so it depends on the object and on the light falling on it.

concepts.term: Viewing an object through a filter
concepts.def: What is seen depends on which wavelengths the object sends towards the filter and which of those the filter transmits. If the filter absorbs every wavelength the object reflects, no light reaches the eye and the object looks black.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes the colours of the visible light spectrum?
options: Each colour is one exact wavelength paired with one exact frequency
Each colour covers its own narrow band of wavelength and frequency
Each colour has its own wavelength band but they share a frequency
All colours share one wavelength band but travel at different speeds
mcqs.explain: This is exactly what the specification states: every colour occupies a small range of wavelengths, with a matching small range of frequencies.

mcqs.q: Red light is at one end of the visible spectrum and violet light at the other. Which comparison is correct?
options: Red light has a longer wavelength and a higher frequency than violet
Red light has the same frequency band as violet but is longer in wavelength
Red light has a shorter wavelength and a lower frequency than violet
Red light has a longer wavelength and a lower frequency than violet
mcqs.explain: Red sits at the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum, and at a fixed wave speed a longer wavelength means a lower frequency.

mcqs.q: A beam of parallel light rays hits a sheet of white paper and leaves in many different directions. Which explanation is correct?
options: Diffuse reflection: the law of reflection does not hold at a rough surface
Absorption: a rough surface takes light in instead of reflecting it back
Specular reflection: the paper is white so it reflects every wavelength
Diffuse reflection: the rough surface reflects the rays in many directions
mcqs.explain: Reflection from a rough surface causes scattering, and the specification calls this diffuse reflection.

mcqs.q: A wall painted with matt paint shows diffuse reflection. Which statement about the individual rays is correct?
options: Each ray still obeys the law of reflection, but the normals point different ways
The law of reflection is broken, because the rays leave at completely random angles
Only a mirror can obey the law of reflection, so painted walls simply scatter light
Each ray shares the same normal, so the reflected beam stays parallel after the wall
mcqs.explain: The surface is uneven, so neighbouring points have normals in different directions and the reflected rays are scattered even though each obeys the law.

mcqs.q: You can see your face in a still pond, but not when the wind puts ripples on it. Why?
options: Rippled water absorbs the light, so almost none of it returns to your eyes
Only a mirror is smooth enough to reflect light well enough to form an image
Still water is smooth and gives specular reflection; ripples scatter the light
Still water reflects the light but rippled water refracts all of it instead
mcqs.explain: A smooth surface reflects in a single direction, forming an image; a rippled surface is rough and causes diffuse reflection.

mcqs.q: How does a green colour filter work?
options: It transmits green light and absorbs the other wavelengths
It adds green colour to whatever light passes through it
It changes the wavelength of the light passing to green
It reflects green light and transmits all other wavelengths
mcqs.explain: This is the specification statement: filters absorb certain wavelengths and transmit others.

mcqs.q: White light is shone through a red filter and then through a green filter onto a screen. What is seen on the screen?
options: Red light, because once light has left the first filter its colour cannot be removed
Green light, because the second filter changes the red light passing through it
No light, because the green filter absorbs the red light the first filter transmits
Yellow light, because the red light and the green filter combine their colours
mcqs.explain: The red filter transmits only red; a green filter absorbs red, so no wavelengths are transmitted and the screen is dark.

mcqs.q: A red rose with green leaves is viewed through a blue filter in white light. How does it appear?
options: The petals appear blue and the leaves appear blue
The petals appear red and the leaves appear black
Both the petals and the leaves appear black
The petals appear black and the leaves stay green
mcqs.explain: The petals reflect red and the leaves reflect green; the blue filter absorbs both, so no light from the rose reaches the eye.

mcqs.q: What determines the colour of an opaque object seen in white light?
options: The wavelengths of light that it reflects most strongly
The wavelengths of light that it absorbs most strongly
The wavelengths of light that pass right through it
The wavelengths of light that it turns into other colours
mcqs.explain: The specification states that colour is determined by which wavelengths are more strongly reflected; the rest are absorbed.

mcqs.q: A jumper appears blue in white light. Which statement describes what the jumper is doing?
options: It absorbs blue light strongly and reflects the other wavelengths
It reflects blue light strongly and absorbs the other wavelengths
It transmits blue light and reflects all the other wavelengths
It reflects every wavelength equally and gives out blue light too
mcqs.explain: Blue is the wavelength band reaching the eye, so it is the one reflected; the wavelengths not reflected are absorbed.

mcqs.q: A book that looks red in white light is placed in a room lit only by green light. How does it look, and why?
options: Red, because the colour belongs to the book and the lighting cannot change it
Green, because the book reflects back whatever light happens to be shone on it
Yellow, because red from the book mixes with green from the lamp in the room
Black, because it absorbs the green light and no red light is there to reflect
mcqs.explain: A red object reflects only red; with no red light present and green light absorbed, no light reaches the eye.

mcqs.q: Why does an object appear white when white light shines on it?
options: Because all of the wavelengths are reflected equally
Because all of the wavelengths pass straight through it
Because it reflects only the white wavelengths of light
Because all of the wavelengths are absorbed equally
mcqs.explain: The specification states that if all wavelengths are reflected equally the object appears white.

mcqs.q: A black surface is placed in a brightly lit room. Which statement is correct?
options: No light is reaching it, which is why it looks black
It transmits all wavelengths, so none comes back out
It absorbs all wavelengths of the light falling on it
It reflects all wavelengths equally but only very weakly
mcqs.explain: The specification states that if all wavelengths are absorbed the object appears black.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a transparent object and a translucent object?
options: Both transmit light equally well, so the two words mean the same thing
Both transmit light, but a translucent object scatters the light it transmits
A transparent object transmits light and a translucent one absorbs it
A translucent object transmits light and a transparent one reflects it
mcqs.explain: Objects that transmit light are either transparent or translucent; scattering is what stops a clear view through a translucent object.

mcqs.q: Frosted glass in a bathroom window lets light into the room, but you cannot see clearly through it. The glass is:
options: translucent, because it transmits the light but scatters it
opaque, because no clear image can be seen through it
transparent, because the light still gets through the glass
translucent, because it absorbs all the light hitting it
mcqs.explain: Light is transmitted, so the glass is not opaque; the scattering is what prevents a clear image.

mcqs.q: A shirt with red and white stripes is viewed in white light through a red filter. What is seen?
options: The red stripes look red and the white stripes stay white as before
All of the shirt looks red, so the stripes can no longer be told apart
All of the shirt looks white, because the filter adds red to the white
The red stripes look black and the white stripes look red instead
mcqs.explain: Red stripes reflect red and white stripes reflect all wavelengths; the filter transmits only red from each, so both look the same red.

mcqs.q: Light from a lamp passes through a piece of blue stained glass. Which explains why the light beyond it is blue?
options: The glass turns the white light into blue light as it passes through
The glass absorbs blue light and transmits the other wavelengths
The glass reflects blue light back and transmits nothing at all
The glass transmits blue light and absorbs the other wavelengths
mcqs.explain: Coloured glass acts as a filter: certain wavelengths are absorbed and the rest are transmitted.
